question: persister
prompt:
Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Here are 5 ideas that were proposed for this question:

1. Sister-cell split assay to recover the pre-treatment state of survivors: Let single cells divide once or twice, physically separate the resulting sister subpopulations, expose one to the targeted drug and keep the other untreated, then use heritable lineage barcodes to trace which untreated sisters correspond to the rare survivors. Transcriptional or chromatin profiling of those retrospectively identified sisters reveals the primed state that existed before any drug was applied.
2. Imaging-based rare-state quantification before and after treatment: Apply highly multiplexed single-molecule RNA imaging or protein immunofluorescence across tens of thousands of untreated cells to detect the rare subpopulations expressing candidate tolerance programs, and quantify how often those marker combinations co-occur in the same cell. Repeating the measurement on survivors tests whether the same program is enriched, distinguishing pre-existing priming from drug-induced adaptation.
3. Longitudinal live imaging of individual cells through the treatment window: Track thousands of single cells with fluorescent reporters for pathway activity, cell-cycle position, and stress response from before drug addition through death or survival, so each cell's fate can be regressed on its own prior dynamics. This directly tests whether features such as slow cycling, signaling pulse frequency, or reporter fluctuation amplitude predict which cells persist.
4. Clonal barcode tracking across repeated treatment and drug-holiday cycles: Barcode a population at high complexity, treat, allow outgrowth, remove drug, and re-treat, sequencing barcode abundances at each step. If the same clones dominate every round the tolerance is heritable and stable; if survivor identity reshuffles between rounds it is a transient, reversible state, and the reshuffling rate estimates how fast cells switch in and out of it.
5. Paired genomic and epigenomic profiling of survivors versus bulk population: Perform single-cell joint chromatin-accessibility and transcriptome assays, plus whole-genome or targeted sequencing, on survivors and matched untreated controls. This separates genetic resistance mutations and copy-number changes from non-genetic chromatin reconfiguration, and identifies the transcription factor motifs whose accessibility changes as cells enter or exit the tolerant state.

A senior expert reviewing them says they are the ideas everyone in the field would propose first. Propose 5 replacement ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that are substantially less obvious but still concrete, scientifically sound, and feasible for a research lab. Do not repeat or lightly modify the ideas above. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Non-genetic Luria–Delbrück fluctuation analysis
ideas.description: Seed many parallel small cultures from few cells, expand them for a varying number of generations, then treat each independently and count survivors, analyzing the across-culture variance-to-mean ratio rather than the mean. The shape of that distribution and its dependence on pre-treatment expansion time yields the state-switching rate and distinguishes pre-existing heritable priming from drug-induced conversion using only colony counts, with no molecular profiling and no assumption about which genes matter.

ideas.title: Per-cell drug exposure and target engagement as the first explanatory variable
ideas.description: Measure intracellular drug concentration in single cells (fluorescent drug analog, efflux-substrate dye, or mass-spectrometry imaging) together with a direct target-occupancy readout such as NanoBRET or a proximal phospho-reporter, in the same cells whose fate is later scored. This tests the mundane but rarely excluded possibility that survivors are simply cells that received or retained less drug, and quantifies how much fate variance remains after pharmacological heterogeneity is accounted for.

ideas.title: Promoter allelic series that changes expression noise at constant mean
ideas.description: Build a panel of synthetic or edited promoters driving a candidate tolerance gene that differ in transcriptional burst size and frequency while matching population-mean expression, then measure survivor frequency across the panel. If survival scales with variance at fixed mean, fluctuation-generated rare states are causally responsible, which no amount of correlative profiling of survivors can establish.

ideas.title: Dual-reporter decomposition of the priming variable into gene-specific versus global noise
ideas.description: Insert two spectrally distinct reporters under identical copies of the candidate priming promoter in the same cell and compare their correlated versus uncorrelated fluctuations, alongside global physiology markers like cell size, ribosome content, and mitochondrial mass. This separates whether the rare tolerant state reflects a gene-specific stochastic program or is a downstream readout of a broader cell-physiological axis, which changes what should be targeted.

ideas.title: Randomizing the microenvironment to test neighborhood-determined survival
ideas.description: Use micropatterned islands, controlled seeding densities, and co-culture with differentially labeled cells to systematically vary each cell's local neighborhood size and composition, plus conditioned-medium and transwell swaps to isolate secreted factors. Comparing survival statistics across these designs tests whether apparent cell-intrinsic rare states are actually stochastic local niches, a confound shared by essentially all dish-based survivor-profiling experiments.
